overview: This file assembles U.S. diplomatic and consular reporting on Japanese merchant-vessel movements during early July 1941, together with confidential paraphrases forwarded to the Navy’s Office of Naval Operations and related commercial correspondence. Reports from Latin America, Japan, and East Asia track arrivals, departures, routes, cancelled sailings, and possible restrictions on voyages to the United States, including the diversion of Japanese cargo to West Coast ports, the absence of bills of health for vessels bound beyond Los Angeles, and the disappearance of an advertised Dairen–U.S. East Coast sailing. The bundle also records three dark-grey, Nazi-flagged ships at Yokohama and contains a freight forwarder’s warning to Secretary Cordell Hull that Japanese shippers appeared to be avoiding New York, followed by the State Department’s acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Norweb on the Sagami Maru at Peruvian ports
subfiles.to: U.S. Secretary of State, Washington; information for the Navy Department
subfiles.about: Reports the Sagami Maru’s arrival at Callao and departure for Kobe by way of Chancay.
subfiles.summary: Norweb reported that the Japanese ship Sagami Maru reached Callao on July 6 after sailing from Valparaíso via Cerro Azul. It departed on July 7 for Kobe via Chancay, and the information was transmitted to the Office of Naval Operations.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Parsloe on the Africa Maru
subfiles.about: Reports the Africa Maru’s brief call at Santos while voyaging from Osaka to Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Parsloe reported that the Japanese steamer Africa Maru arrived at Santos from Osaka on July 5. It sailed for Buenos Aires on July 6, and the restricted telegram was paraphrased for OPNAV.

subfiles.title: Confidential Navy paraphrase of the Africa Maru report
subfiles.about: Paraphrases Parsloe’s report that the Africa Maru had left Santos for Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: This internal transmission restates the Santos telegram in altered language for confidential delivery to the Navy. It records that the Africa Maru had arrived from Osaka on July 5 and left Santos for Buenos Aires the following day.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Linnell on the Daini Ogura and Kuroshio tankers
subfiles.about: Reports two Japanese tanker departures for ports in California.
subfiles.summary: Linnell stated that the tanker Daini Ogura sailed for San Francisco on July 2. The tanker Kuroshio was reportedly underway from Niigata to San Pedro, and the restricted report was paraphrased for the Navy.

subfiles.title: Confidential Navy paraphrase of Japanese tanker departures
subfiles.about: Restates Linnell’s report on the Kuroshio and Daini Ogura departures for California.
subfiles.summary: The State Department paraphrase says that the Kuroshio had reportedly departed Niigata for San Pedro. It also records that the Daini Ogura left for San Francisco on July 2.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Warner on restrictions affecting U.S.-bound Japanese ships
subfiles.about: Reports the suspension of bills of health and the absence of July sailings beyond Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Warner reported that no bills of health had been granted since June 26 to Japanese vessels bound for the United States. No sailings beyond Los Angeles were scheduled during July, suggesting a contraction or diversion of Japanese service to American ports.

subfiles.title: Letter from H. S. Dorf and Company on Japanese ships avoiding New York
subfiles.from: H. S. Dorf and Company, Incorporated
subfiles.to: Cordell H. Hull, U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Conveys importers’ reports that Japanese shippers intended to discharge cargo only at U.S. West Coast ports.
subfiles.summary: The freight-forwarding firm reported that several Japanese importers had telephoned during the preceding two weeks to say that shippers in Japan did not intend to send their vessels to New York. Their cargo would instead be discharged at San Francisco, Seattle, or Los Angeles. The firm could not explain the change but believed the information might be significant to the State Department.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment to H. S. Dorf
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Dorf’s letter concerning reported Japanese merchant-vessel movements.
subfiles.summary: Writing on Secretary Hull’s behalf, Adams thanked Dorf for bringing the shipping information to the Department’s attention. The page is identified as a true copy of the signed original and bears Division of Far Eastern Affairs processing notations.

subfiles.title: Duplicate State Department acknowledgment to H. S. Dorf
subfiles.about: Preserves a second file copy of the acknowledgment of Dorf’s shipping report.
subfiles.summary: This page duplicates Adams’s July 15 acknowledgment of Dorf’s July 5 letter. It again records Secretary Hull’s appreciation for the information about Japanese merchant-vessel movements and is marked as a true copy.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Grew relaying Chase on the planned Kinryu Maru sailing
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, relaying Chase at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports that a previously advertised Kinryu Maru sailing from Dairen to U.S. East Coast ports disappeared from local schedules.
subfiles.summary: Grew relayed Chase’s July 7 report from Dairen concerning the Osaka Shosen Kaisha vessel Kinryu Maru. Although its July 16 departure for United States East Coast ports had appeared daily in local schedules, the advertisement was omitted from the previous day’s newspapers. Chase also repeated the report by airmail to Kobe.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Grew’s Kinryu Maru telegram
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, relaying Chase at Dairen
subfiles.about: Duplicates the report about the disappearance of the Kinryu Maru’s advertised U.S.-bound sailing.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the telegram preserved on page 10, including the advertised July 16 departure from Dairen and the omission of that voyage from the latest newspaper schedule. A later notation indicates that this copy was sent or processed on November 22, 1941.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Hornibrook on the Kiyokawa Maru
subfiles.about: Reports the planned departure of the Japanese merchant vessel Kiyokawa Maru from Puntarenas for Balboa.
subfiles.summary: Hornibrook reported that the Japanese merchant vessel Kiyokawa Maru would sail from Puntarenas for Balboa on the night of July 7. The restricted message was paraphrased and sent to OPNAV early on July 8.

subfiles.title: Confidential Navy paraphrase of the Kiyokawa Maru report
subfiles.about: Restates Hornibrook’s report of the Kiyokawa Maru’s departure from Puntarenas for Balboa.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase identifies the Kiyokawa Maru as a Japanese merchantman. It says that the vessel would leave Puntarenas for Balboa that night and was transmitted under confidential classification.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Linnell on the Kasima and Nazi-flagged ships
subfiles.about: Reports the Kasima’s voyage toward Australia and the arrival of three dark-grey, Nazi-flagged vessels at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Linnell reported that the Kasima left on July 3 for Australia by way of Manila and Davao. On the same day, three ships painted dark grey and flying Nazi flags arrived at Yokohama. The restricted telegram was paraphrased for the Navy.

subfiles.title: Confidential Navy paraphrase of the Yokohama ship report
subfiles.about: Restates Linnell’s report on three Nazi-flagged ships and the Kasima’s departure.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase records the July 3 arrival at Yokohama of three dark-grey ships flying Nazi flags. It also reports that the Kasima sailed the same day for Australia via Manila and Davao.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Parsloe on the Brisbane Maru
subfiles.about: Reports the Brisbane Maru’s arrival from Cape Town and its projected multi-port voyage to Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Parsloe reported that the Japanese motor ship Brisbane Maru arrived at Santos from Cape Town on July 7. It was to sail on July 8 for Kobe via Montevideo, Buenos Aires, the Panama Canal, and Los Angeles, and the report was paraphrased for OPNAV.

subfiles.title: Confidential Navy paraphrase of the Brisbane Maru report
subfiles.about: Restates the Brisbane Maru’s arrival and intended route from Santos to Kobe.
subfiles.summary: The State Department paraphrase reports that the Brisbane Maru arrived from Cape Town on July 7. It was sailing for Montevideo, Buenos Aires, the Panama Canal, Los Angeles, and Kobe, providing the Navy with its projected route across the Atlantic and Pacific.

interest: The file provides an unusually granular snapshot of how the State Department and Navy monitored Japanese commercial shipping through a worldwide network of consular posts immediately before the major deterioration in U.S.–Japanese relations later in July 1941. Its paired original telegrams and carefully reworded Navy versions document the mechanics of handling restricted maritime intelligence, while the Dorf correspondence shows how information from private importers and freight forwarders entered official channels. Taken together, the cancellation indicators, health-document restrictions, avoidance of New York, and concentration on West Coast ports may help historians reconstruct changing Japanese shipping policy and contemporary American perceptions of impending disruption.
